instruction.name: xvld
instruction.description: Read whole vector from memory address `addr + offset`, save the data into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. Note that you can use this intrinsic to load floating point vectors, even though the return type represents integer vectors.

experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 6666 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 9 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; st.d $r0, $r20, 0; st.d $r0, $r20, 8' --asm 'xvld $xr0, $r20, 0; xvpickve2gr.d $r4, $xr0, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'

latencies.notes: rj -> vd. Chain: xvld reading at the carried base, then xvpickve2gr.d (6 cycles) and add.d (1 cycle) to advance the base; the 7-cycle closure is subtracted. L1D hit. Three independent runs, raw cycle spread 12.00-12.00. Measured on 2026-11-17 on LA464, core 0.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvld $xr0, $r20, 0; xvld $xr1, $r20, 32; xvld $xr2, $r20, 64; xvld $xr3, $r20, 96; xvld $xr4, $r20, 128; xvld $xr5, $r20, 160; xvld $xr6, $r20, 192; xvld $xr7, $r20, 224
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'xvld $xr0, $r20, 0; xvld $xr1, $r20, 32; xvld $xr2, $r20, 64; xvld $xr3, $r20, 96; xvld $xr4, $r20, 128; xvld $xr5, $r20, 160; xvld $xr6, $r20, 192; xvld $xr7, $r20, 224'

notes: No destination data dependency; latency is not defined. Throughput only.
